subject: Onboarding: SLA evidence & portal handoff
messages:
From: Megan Ortiz <megan@civiccart.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@civiccart.com
Date: 2026-11-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding: SLA evidence & portal handoff

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Procurement asked us to get the formal evidence package and a short witness plan so we can sign off on the SLA thresholds (p50/p95 latency and steady-state throughput). I've attached our load profile (civiccart-loadspecs.csv) — it reflects typical traffic for our checkout flows (mostly short text prompts, average 64 tokens).

Can Redwood provide: 1) the run artifacts (raw logs / summarized latency histogram), 2) a short witness run plan so our ops can observe, and 3) confirmation of fallback behavior if capacity constraints appear during the run?

We'd like to schedule the witness window next week (Nov 23–25) in the 9–13 PST window if possible. Procurement is holding off signature until they see the evidence package.

Thanks,
Megan Ortiz
Head of Infrastructure 
CivicCart

Attachment: civiccart-loadspecs.csv

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Megan Ortiz <megan@civiccart.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding: SLA evidence & portal handoff

Megan — thanks for the clear ask and the load spec. Tagging Monica and Dev to own the evidence and witness plan.

High level: we'll produce a compact evidence bundle (latency histograms, request/response samples, token-level cost breakdown) and run a Redwood-hosted witness session you can join. Proposed plan (high level):
- Pre-run: we validate the load spec and convert to runner configuration (same sequence length distribution + warmup).
- Witness run: 30 minute steady-state run at your 90th percentile target throughput, followed by a 10 minute spike test. We’ll stream logs to a shared Drive link.
- Artifacts: p50/p95/p99 histograms, per-endpoint qps, error rate, and a short README describing the environment (model, quantization, GPU type, batch config).
- Fallback behavior: readout of routing policy — if Dedicated pool saturates we will route to a compatible variant and mark requests with fallback tag in traces.

I've attached our standard acceptance checklist for onboarding (acceptance-checklist-v1.xlsx) and will export the run artifacts into a tarball after the session. Dev, can you confirm the runner config and whether the 9–13 PST windows on Nov 23–25 work?

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
redwood.com

Attachment: acceptance-checklist-v1.xlsx

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Megan Ortiz <megan@civiccart.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T11:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding: SLA evidence & portal handoff

Thanks Laura — a couple of quick acceptance criteria items from CS to make it explicit for procurement:
- Steady-state throughput: 450 qps sustained (±5%) for 30m with <0.5% 5xx errors.
- Tail latency: p95 <= 220ms for API-response time (end-to-end call).
- Regression check: sampled prompts (we'll use 250 prompts from your prod set) must not show hallucination or significant quality drop vs baseline A/B evaluation (we'll share the eval IDs).

We'll also need the raw histograms (json or csv) and a short summary CSV with the aggregated metrics. If those pass, procurement will accept the SLA and sign.

If Nov 23 is a US holiday for you, we can do Nov 24/25; otherwise the 23rd morning works for CivicCart specifically.

-Monica
Monica Patel
Sr. Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Megan Ortiz <megan@civiccart.com>
Date: 2026-11-19T09:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding: SLA evidence & portal handoff

Hi all — I ran a dry run against a staging variant yesterday matching the CivicCart load spec. Summary (high level):
- Runner: redwood-runner v2.8 (continuous batching enabled, KV cache warm).
- Model: openfast-13b (8-bit quantized) on Nvidia A40 equivalent nodes.
- Configuration: batch_target=32, max_latency_ms=500, autoscale_burst=20%.

Key metrics from the 30m steady-state window (see attached tarball for full logs):
- Target throughput: 450 qps 
- Observed steady throughput: 452 qps (mean)
- Error rate (5xx): 0.32% (mostly transient LB retries)
- Latency (API end-to-end): p50=42ms, p95=198ms, p99=420ms
- Token-level cost: ~0.0009 USD/token (summarized)

Notes: p95 is under the requested 220ms target. The p99 spikes are associated with cold KV misses during an induced cache eviction; we can mitigate by increasing cache retention or slightly adjusting batch_target. The fallback behavior test (routing to variant-b) during a simulated pool saturation worked and requests were tagged with fallback=true in traces.

Artifacts included in redwood-loadproof-20261117.tar.gz: latency_histograms.json, request_samples.jsonl, runner_config.yaml, aggregated_metrics.csv. I also exported a condensed evidence CSV (aggregated_metrics.csv) for procurement review.

Proposed witness plan (more concrete):
1) Pre-check (15m): confirm test config and Drive link.
2) Witness run (30m): run at 450 qps steady, streaming metrics to the Drive.
3) Spike test (10m): 3x short spikes to validate graceful degradation.
4) Post-run (15m): quick readout with screenshots and CSV drop.

Can we lock Nov 24 09:30 PST for the witness run? That avoids the Nov 23 holiday in your region.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Implementation Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-loadproof-20261117.tar.gz

From: Megan Ortiz <megan@civiccart.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, procurement@civiccart.com
Date: 2026-11-20T16:34:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding: SLA evidence & portal handoff

Laura / Dev / Monica — this is perfect, thank you. Nov 24 09:30 PST works for our ops and procurement. A couple quick clarifications before the run: 
- For the regression check, can you confirm the eval IDs you'll use for sampling? Procurement wants the eval artifact name in the evidence bundle so they can cross-reference.
- On the fallback tagging: is the fallback=true tag sent downstream in the request headers or only present in Redwood traces? We need an explicit header to correlate with our downstream logging.

If we get those two items, procurement is ready to finalize the PO immediately after the readout. I'll plan to join the witness run and ask procurement to standby.

Megan Ortiz
Head of Infrastructure, CivicCart
megan@civiccart.com
